project.description: For finite I and a commutative topological group E, ContinuousMonoidHom.intPiEvalEquiv I E identifies continuous homomorphisms from the original Multiplicative (I → ℤ) with I → E, with the compact-open topology. Evaluation uses the standard integer generators; reconstruction is the finite product of integer powers, including the empty index. Domain and coordinate transports assemble the existing finite-product, integer and type-tag equivalences, without local compactness, separation, nonemptiness or a discrete-target assumption. Fixed evaluation defines PontryaginDual.evalHom on every monoid with a topology, into its entire compact-open bidual. Canonical bidual equivalences of two factors, with their pointwise evaluation laws, give the explicit constructor PontryaginDual.prodEvalEquiv without additional source hypotheses. The additive real plane uses the two real factor equivalences and ContinuousMulEquiv.prodMultiplicative, which lifts Mathlib's algebraic tagged-product equivalence under addition and topologies alone. For finite dependent products, ContinuousMonoidHom.piEquiv and PontryaginDual.piEquiv restrict to the coordinates, and PontryaginDual.piEvalEquiv constructs canonical biduality from canonical factor equivalences. The arbitrary-index tag lift ContinuousMulEquiv.piMultiplicative gives PontryaginDual.realPiEvalEquiv on Multiplicative (I → ℝ) for finite I, including the empty index. All source topologies and algebraic structures are the original ones. Generator evaluation also identifies the compact-open space of continuous homomorphisms from Multiplicative ℤ with any topological group E via ContinuousMonoidHom.intEvalHomeomorph E. For commutative E, ContinuousMonoidHom.intEvalEquiv E is a continuous multiplicative equivalence with the same homeomorphism. Its Circle specialization identifies PontryaginDual (Multiplicative ℤ) with Circle, without local compactness or Hausdorff hypotheses in the generic result. Canonical evaluation sends a monoid A with a topology continuously into its compact-open Pontryagin bidual under LocallyCompactPair A Circle. Evaluation is natural under continuous monoid homomorphisms; evaluation on the dual is a section of the dual of evaluation when the dual also forms a locally compact pair with Circle. Every continuous character of the additive real line has a unique period-one Fourier frequency. The Fourier parametrization is an equivalence for the original compact-open topology, and canonical real bidual evaluation is a continuous multiplicative equivalence. No general locally compact abelian reflexivity theorem is asserted. Restriction identifies the compact-open circle dual of a binary product with the product of the factor duals, for arbitrary monoids with topologies. The inverse multiplies the factor character values; the equivalence is natural under product maps and needs no source-operation continuity, local compactness or separation. The generic continuous-hom coproduct equivalence uses a commutative topological-group target; its algebraic restriction universal property only needs a commutative monoid target with continuous multiplication. In a reduced monoid with zero, every nonzero natural exponent m satisfies a ^ m * b = 0 iff a * b = 0 and a * b ^ m = 0 iff a * b = 0. The lemmas pow_mul_eq_zero_iff and mul_pow_eq_zero_iff require only MonoidWithZero and IsReduced, without commutativity, cancellation, absence of zero divisors or nontriviality. The positive-exponent condition is essential. For monoids M and N, let S : Set M contain, for each x : M, a finite indexed family of powers x ^ (e i) with gcd one. In any common carrier F with FunLike F M N and MulHomClass F M N, fixed g h : F satisfy Set.EqOn g h S iff g = h whenever every g x is left-regular. The source, target, map-carrier and index universes are independent; both the finite index set and exponent function may depend on x. The additive form uses AddHomClass, additive monoids and natural multiples. No unit-preserving map class, regularity of h, algebra on S, global cancellation, commutativity, finite or nonempty index type, or positivity assumption is required. Zero and repeated exponents are allowed. The indexed image criterion is the range specialization, followed by the Nat/id criterion. For f : A →* M with only MulOne A and monoids M and N, suppose each x : M admits s : Finset ι and e : ι → ℕ with s.gcd e = 1 and x ^ (e i) in Set.range f for every i in s. For fixed g, h : M →* N, right-regularity of every g x gives g.comp f = h.comp f iff g = h. The four universes are independent, and both s and e may depend on x. No regularity of h, global cancellation, commutativity, surjectivity, finite or nonempty index type, or positivity assumption is required. The same proof gives the additive form with AddZero A, additive monoids and natural multiples. For f : A →* M with only MulOne A and monoids M and N, suppose each x : M admits s : Finset ι and e : ι → ℕ with s.gcd e = 1 and x ^ (e i) in Set.range f for every i in s. For fixed g, h : M →* N, left-regularity of every g x gives g.comp f = h.comp f iff g = h. The four universes are independent; both s and e may depend on x. No regularity of h, global cancellation, commutativity, surjectivity, finite or nonempty index type, decidable equality or positivity is needed. The same proof gives the additive form with AddZero A and natural multiples. The indexed image criterion specializes the set criterion to the range, and the finite-natural-exponent API is its Nat/id specialization. Zero and repeated exponents are allowed; singleton exponent one is legal, while empty or all-zero families cannot have gcd one. Coprime-pair and consecutive-power restriction, and the latter's left-cancellative injectivity form, are specializations. In any monoid, a left-regular element a and arbitrary b have equal powers at the gcd of a finite family of natural exponents if and only if their powers agree at every selected exponent. Gcd one gives a = b. The additive images require only an additive monoid and injective left addition by a. Neither statement requires regularity of b, global cancellation, commutativity, nonempty families or positive exponents. Every topological group has a Hausdorff, totally disconnected quotient by its identity component, without separation or local compactness of the original group. Continuous homomorphisms to totally disconnected groups equipped with a topology factor uniquely through this quotient; the target operations need not be continuous. Every identity neighborhood in a locally compact totally disconnected topological group contains a compact open subgroup. The open left-translation stabilizer of any compact open set provides the construction; compactness of that subgroup follows when the set contains the identity. For a continuous homomorphism from a nonarchimedean group, a subgroup-free target identity neighborhood forces an open kernel, without source compactness, commutativity or target separation. An open kernel makes a group homomorphism locally constant even without continuity or a target topology. With compact source, the image and kernel quotient are finite, the quotient is discrete, and Mathlib's canonical kernel lift uniquely factors the map. Circle's centered half-arc gives the character case. In a compact Hausdorff commutative topological group with an abstractly finitely generated dense subgroup, every positive-power range has finite index and is open. Every abstract finite-index subgroup is open without assuming it closed; the additive versions use natural-number scalars. In a locally compact topological group, the identity component is the intersection of all open subgroups. Under a continuous open surjective group homomorphism from a locally compact source, the closure of its identity-component image equals the target identity component. Neither result requires Hausdorffness of the original groups. An open quotient map from a compact Hausdorff totally disconnected space to a Hausdorff space has totally disconnected target, without group structure, injectivity or a local-compactness assumption on the target. An open quotient group homomorphism from a locally compact totally disconnected group to a Hausdorff group has the same conclusion. The compact-open space of continuous maps from any compact space to a discrete space is discrete, without Hausdorffness or nonemptiness. Every discrete-valued continuous map on a compact topological group descends through an open normal subgroup to its finite discrete quotient, without total disconnectedness, commutativity or a homomorphism condition. On an arbitrary power I → G of a compact topological group, every such map factors through s → G / N for a finite set s of coordinates and one open normal subgroup N of G. Only this selected stage is asserted to be finite and discrete, not the full quotient power over I. The index, group and target universes are independent. No finiteness of I or Y, algebraic structure on Y, additional nonemptiness, Hausdorffness or profinite hypothesis is needed. Every open normal subgroup of a dependent product of groups with arbitrary topologies contains a cylinder defined by open normal subgroups in finitely many factors. For a constant family, one subgroup controls all selected coordinates; the remaining coordinates are unrestricted. These containment statements need no continuity of operations, compactness, separation or finiteness of the index type. Every continuous group homomorphism from an arbitrary dependent product of groups equipped with topologies to a discrete group factors through open normal quotients of finitely many coordinates. Each selected canonical quotient and their product are discrete. Source operations need not be continuous; neither the index nor target needs to be finite. Compact factors make these selected quotients and their product finite. The canonical selected projection needs only normal subgroups and has an application, kernel, surjectivity and monoid-target unique descent API, the latter conditional on the projection being a quotient map. For any category and monoid-valued diagram with arbitrary stage topologies, compatible sections have continuous coordinate projections and an initial topology. Compatible continuous monoid homomorphisms from any monoid equipped with a topology lift uniquely to sections and form an equivalent family API; group diagrams have a continuous projection extending the algebraic one. An exactness criterion for the finite cyclic norm of an endomorphism of an additive commutative group, requiring a positive natural period m with sigma^m = 1 (not necessarily exact order), injective multiplication by that same m, and elementwise lifting of fixed classes modulo mA. For an arbitrary subgroup H of a group G with a supplied topology and continuous fixed left translations (ContinuousConstSMul G G), openness is equivalent to discreteness of the canonical left-coset quotient G / H, and closedness is equivalent to its T1 property. Clopenness is equivalent to openness without an index assumption. At finite index, openness, closedness and clopenness are equivalent, without compactness. Compactness is needed only to deduce finite index from openness. No normality, right continuity, joint multiplication, continuous inversion or ambient separation is required. The existing quotient and coinduced topology are unchanged. For any group G and arbitrary subgroups H and K, the canonical left-coset G-sets G / H and G / K are isomorphic exactly when H and K are conjugate. An equality H = gKg⁻¹ gives right translation [z] ↦ [z * g], with inverse [z] ↦ [z * g⁻¹]. No finiteness, normality or topological assumption is needed. For finitely generated abelian groups, surjectivity of the n-scalar map with n ≥ 2 forces finiteness and coprimality with Nat.card A and yields a uniform two-sided integer-scalar inverse; the converse characterizes surjectivity and bijectivity of that scalar map. For representations of a monoid over a semiring on their given additive commutative monoid modules, fixed submodules commute with binary and arbitrary indexed products, including infinite and empty index types. Canonical linear equivalences split coordinates and are natural in supplied intertwining maps. They use representation-independent submodule-product splittings; the indexed splitting linearly enriches Mathlib's subtype-Pi equivalence. For a group acting pretransitively on a finite nonempty set X, the fixed submodule of its permutation representation over any semiring R is linearly equivalent to R. The forward map has coefficient r at every point, and the inverse evaluates at any point. The group need not be finite; the semiring may be zero or noncommutative. A nonzero fixed vector forces the carrier to be finite, and the fixed submodule is bottom on infinite carriers. An element x of a commutative domain A integral over a commutative ring R has a finite orbit under any monoid M acting on A by semiring endomorphisms that commute with R-scalars. The three universes are independent; no action on R, injective scalar map, faithful action, integrality of all of A, or group or finiteness assumption on M is required.

highlights.statement: For every finitely generated discrete group G and locally compact Hausdorff topological group D, the space of continuous homomorphisms G → D with the compact-open topology is locally compact.

headlines.text: Every abelian group has enough homomorphisms into the standard complex unit circle to separate distinct elements. A circle-valued homomorphism on any subgroup extends to the whole group. For a group with its given discrete topology, the same algebraic characters are continuous, and evaluation into the product indexed by all continuous circle characters is injective. This is a separation result, not surjectivity or a topological embedding into the compact-open bidual.

See [subgroup extension](https://github.com/FormalFrontier/group-theory/blob/cad97f1a1920e3c68d41ec2d689cde51231b5a31/GroupTheory/Character/Extension.lean), [cyclic characters](https://github.com/FormalFrontier/group-theory/blob/cad97f1a1920e3c68d41ec2d689cde51231b5a31/GroupTheory/Character/Cyclic.lean), and [separation and evaluation](https://github.com/FormalFrontier/group-theory/blob/cad97f1a1920e3c68d41ec2d689cde51231b5a31/GroupTheory/Character/Separation.lean).

`M` and a compact Hausdorff unital magma `D` with continuous multiplication,
`ContinuousMap.isCompact_mulOneHomLocus` proves compactness of the full locus
`{f : C(M, D) | f 1 = 1 ∧ ∀ x y, f (x * y) = f x * f y}` in the compact-open
topology. No associativity or finite generation is needed. For monoids,
`ContinuousMonoidHom.homeoMulOneHomLocus` identifies its canonical subspace
with `M →ₜ* D`, preserving the continuous-map data in both directions; this
identification needs only monoids with their given topologies. See
[`ContinuousMonoidHom.Compact`](https://github.com/FormalFrontier/group-theory/blob/cad97f1a1920e3c68d41ec2d689cde51231b5a31/GroupTheory/Topology/Algebra/ContinuousMonoidHom/Compact.lean).

headlines.title: Finite-support product homomorphisms
headlines.text:
For arbitrary topologized groups `G i` and
a commutative group `D` with continuous multiplication and no small subgroups,
continuous homomorphisms `(∀ i, G i) →ₜ* D` are canonically equivalent as commutative
monoids to finitely supported families of continuous coordinate homomorphisms.
[Module](https://github.com/FormalFrontier/group-theory/blob/cad97f1a1920e3c68d41ec2d689cde51231b5a31/GroupTheory/Topology/Algebra/ContinuousMonoidHom/ProductDecomposition.lean)
(`ContinuousMonoidHom.productDecomposition`).

headlines.title: Groups with a given uniformity and no small subgroups pass this property to their full uniform function spaces, without continuous group …
headlines.text:
Groups with a given uniformity and no small subgroups pass this property to
their full uniform function spaces, without continuous group operations.
An arbitrary family of ordinary homomorphisms from a product of groups into
such a group, equicontinuous at the identity, kills one common
finite-coordinate subgroup, including all infinite off-coordinate tails.
See [`UniformFun`](https://github.com/FormalFrontier/group-theory/blob/cad97f1a1920e3c68d41ec2d689cde51231b5a31/GroupTheory/Topology/Algebra/Group/NoSmallSubgroups/UniformFun.lean)
and [`EquicontinuousFiniteCoordinates`](https://github.com/FormalFrontier/group-theory/blob/cad97f1a1920e3c68d41ec2d689cde51231b5a31/GroupTheory/Topology/Algebra/ContinuousMonoidHom/EquicontinuousFiniteCoordinates.lean).

headlines.title: Finite-coordinate factorization
headlines.text:
A homomorphism from an arbitrary product of
groups, continuous at the identity, into a group with no small subgroups kills
every element equal to the identity on a suitable finite set of coordinates.
Globally continuous homomorphisms factor continuously through that finite product,
uniquely for the chosen finite set. No continuity of group operations is required.
See [`FiniteCoordinates`](https://github.com/FormalFrontier/group-theory/blob/cad97f1a1920e3c68d41ec2d689cde51231b5a31/GroupTheory/Topology/Algebra/ContinuousMonoidHom/FiniteCoordinates.lean).

headlines.title: Real seminormed spaces and no small subgroups
headlines.text:
A real seminormed space's
additive group has no small subgroups if and only if its seminorm topology is
Hausdorff. In particular, every real normed space has no small subgroups, without
completeness or finite-dimensionality hypotheses. See
[`NormedSpace.lean`](https://github.com/FormalFrontier/group-theory/blob/cad97f1a1920e3c68d41ec2d689cde51231b5a31/GroupTheory/Topology/Algebra/Group/NoSmallSubgroups/NormedSpace.lean).

headlines.title: No small subgroups and compact-source hom spaces
headlines.text:
`NoSmallSubgroups G` means that some identity neighborhood contains no
nontrivial subgroup. Its neighborhood and positive-powers APIs include an
open inversion-symmetric identity neighborhood when inversion is continuous.
For a compact monoid `M` with a topology and a commutative topological group
`G` with no small subgroups,
`ContinuousMonoidHom.discreteTopology_of_noSmallSubgroups` proves
`DiscreteTopology (M →ₜ* G)` for the compact-open topology.
`Circle.noSmallSubgroups` gives the canonical instance using Mathlib's arc
`Circle.centeredArc (Real.pi / 2)` and its existing powers criterion. See
[`Group.NoSmallSubgroups`](https://github.com/FormalFrontier/group-theory/blob/cad97f1a1920e3c68d41ec2d689cde51231b5a31/GroupTheory/Topology/Algebra/Group/NoSmallSubgroups.lean),
[`ContinuousMonoidHom.NoSmallSubgroups`](https://github.com/FormalFrontier/group-theory/blob/cad97f1a1920e3c68d41ec2d689cde51231b5a31/GroupTheory/Topology/Algebra/ContinuousMonoidHom/NoSmallSubgroups.lean)
and [`Group.NoSmallSubgroups.Circle`](https://github.com/FormalFrontier/group-theory/blob/cad97f1a1920e3c68d41ec2d689cde51231b5a31/GroupTheory/Topology/Algebra/Group/NoSmallSubgroups/Circle.lean).

headlines.title: No small subgroups is local under open embeddings
headlines.text:
For groups `G`, `H` with their original arbitrary topologies, an injective
open homomorphism `f : G →* H` sends `NoSmallSubgroups G` to
`NoSmallSubgroups H`; neither operation continuity nor continuity of `f`
is required. If `f` is continuous at one, the two properties are equivalent.
In particular they are equivalent under open embeddings and between an
open subgroup and its ambient group. The API uses this library's existing
definition and reverse transport together with Mathlib's subgroup and
topological embedding APIs. See
[`Group.NoSmallSubgroups.OpenMap`](https://github.com/FormalFrontier/group-theory/blob/cad97f1a1920e3c68d41ec2d689cde51231b5a31/GroupTheory/Topology/Algebra/Group/NoSmallSubgroups/OpenMap.lean).

headlines.title: No small subgroups under open homomorphisms
headlines.text:
Let `G` be a topological
group, `H` a group with a topology, and `f : G →* H` an open homomorphism
whose kernel has the discrete topology induced from `G`. If `G` has no small
subgroups, then so does `H`; neither continuity of `f`, continuous operations
on `H`, nor surjectivity is required. If `f` is also continuous at the identity,
`G` has no small subgroups if and only if `H` does. See
[`NoSmallSubgroups.of_isOpenMap`](https://github.com/FormalFrontier/group-theory/blob/cad97f1a1920e3c68d41ec2d689cde51231b5a31/GroupTheory/Topology/Algebra/Group/NoSmallSubgroups/OpenMap.lean)
and [`MonoidHom.noSmallSubgroups_iff_of_isOpenMap`](https://github.com/FormalFrontier/group-theory/blob/cad97f1a1920e3c68d41ec2d689cde51231b5a31/GroupTheory/Topology/Algebra/Group/NoSmallSubgroups/OpenMap.lean).

headlines.title: No small subgroups in totally disconnected groups
headlines.text:
For a totally
disconnected topological group `G` in which each point admits a compact
neighborhood (`WeaklyLocallyCompactSpace G`),
`noSmallSubgroups_iff_discreteTopology` states
`NoSmallSubgroups G ↔ DiscreteTopology G`. For a compact totally disconnected
topological group, `noSmallSubgroups_iff_finite` states
`NoSmallSubgroups G ↔ Finite G`. These criteria concern the given topology;
no commutativity, nontriviality or separate Hausdorff hypothesis is required.
The open-subgroup argument is classical van Dantzig theory. See
[`Group.NoSmallSubgroups.TotallyDisconnected`](https://github.com/FormalFrontier/group-theory/blob/cad97f1a1920e3c68d41ec2d689cde51231b5a31/GroupTheory/Topology/Algebra/Group/NoSmallSubgroups/TotallyDisconnected.lean)
and the [NSS and discreteness guide](https://github.com/FormalFrontier/group-theory/blob/cad97f1a1920e3c68d41ec2d689cde51231b5a31/docs/NoSmallSubgroups.md) for the statements,
proof ideas and formalization credits.

headlines.title: Locally compact homomorphism spaces
headlines.text:
Let `G` be a finitely generated
discrete group and `D` a locally compact monoid with a topology and jointly
continuous multiplication. If `IsClosed ({1} : Set D)`, then
`ContinuousMonoidHom.locallyCompactSpace_of_fg_of_isClosed_one` proves
`LocallyCompactSpace (G →ₜ* D)` for the original compact-open topology.
No group structure, commutativity, continuous inversion or separation axiom
is assumed on `D`. The proof uses the canonical units lift and this library's
existing group-target local-compactness theorem. See
[`ContinuousMonoidHom.LocallyCompact`](https://github.com/FormalFrontier/group-theory/blob/cad97f1a1920e3c68d41ec2d689cde51231b5a31/GroupTheory/Topology/Algebra/ContinuousMonoidHom/LocallyCompact.lean)
and [`ContinuousMonoidHom.Units`](https://github.com/FormalFrontier/group-theory/blob/cad97f1a1920e3c68d41ec2d689cde51231b5a31/GroupTheory/Topology/Algebra/ContinuousMonoidHom/Units.lean).

headlines.title: Pointwise products of dependent finitely supported functions
headlines.text:
`DFinsupp.pointwiseMul` gives a non-instance `Mul (Π₀ i, β i)` whenever
each fibre is a `MulZeroClass`; evaluation multiplies the two coefficients.
Singles at distinct indices have zero product, and product support is contained
in the intersection of the supports. No associativity, unit or finite index is
required. `Finsupp.toDFinsupp_mul` recovers the ordinary pointwise product
without decidability assumptions. Independently,
`Finsupp.toDFinsupp_pointwise_smul` compares function-valued scalar actions
using only a zero-preserving coefficient action. These data are selected
explicitly, without changing the graded multiplication on `DirectSum`.
See [`DFinsupp.Pointwise`](https://github.com/FormalFrontier/group-theory/blob/cad97f1a1920e3c68d41ec2d689cde51231b5a31/GroupTheory/DFinsupp/Pointwise.lean),
[`Finsupp.Pointwise`](https://github.com/FormalFrontier/group-theory/blob/cad97f1a1920e3c68d41ec2d689cde51231b5a31/GroupTheory/Finsupp/Pointwise.lean) and
[`Finsupp.PointwiseScalar`](https://github.com/FormalFrontier/group-theory/blob/cad97f1a1920e3c68d41ec2d689cde51231b5a31/GroupTheory/Finsupp/PointwiseScalar.lean).

headlines.title: Surjectivity of bidual evaluation for discrete groups
headlines.text:
For every discrete
group `A`, not necessarily commutative,
`PontryaginDual.eval_surjective_of_discrete A` makes the canonical map
`PontryaginDual.eval A : A →ₜ* PontryaginDual (PontryaginDual A)` surjective.
This does not assert injectivity or reflexivity for noncommutative groups. See
[`PontryaginDual.Discrete.Surjective`](https://github.com/FormalFrontier/group-theory/blob/cad97f1a1920e3c68d41ec2d689cde51231b5a31/GroupTheory/Topology/PontryaginDual/Discrete/Surjective.lean).

headlines.title: Canonical biduality for discrete abelian groups
headlines.text:
For every `A : Type u`
with `[CommGroup A] [TopologicalSpace A] [DiscreteTopology A]`,
`PontryaginDual.evalEquivOfDiscrete A` is a continuous multiplicative
equivalence `A ≃ₜ* PontryaginDual (PontryaginDual A)` with the original
compact-open topologies. Its forward map is exactly `PontryaginDual.evalHom A`.
The inverse obeys both inverse laws and is characterized by
`χ ((PontryaginDual.evalEquivOfDiscrete A).symm Φ) = Φ χ`.
Both directions are natural for continuous homomorphisms between discrete
abelian groups in independent universes. No finiteness or countability
assumption is needed, and the trivial group is included. See
[`PontryaginDual.Discrete.Equivalence`](https://github.com/FormalFrontier/group-theory/blob/cad97f1a1920e3c68d41ec2d689cde51231b5a31/GroupTheory/Topology/PontryaginDual/Discrete/Equivalence.lean).

For a finite index type `I` and a commutative topological group `E`,
[`ContinuousMonoidHom.intPiEvalEquiv I E`](https://github.com/FormalFrontier/group-theory/blob/cad97f1a1920e3c68d41ec2d689cde51231b5a31/GroupTheory/Topology/Algebra/ContinuousMonoidHom/Int/Pi.lean)
identifies the compact-open space `Multiplicative (I → ℤ) →ₜ* E` with `I → E`
by evaluation on the standard integer generators. Its inverse sends `c` to
`ofAdd n ↦ ∏ i, c i ^ n i` and retains the existing finite coproduct of
integer-power homomorphisms. The source has its original product and type-tag
topologies. The empty index is included; no nonemptiness, source local
compactness, separation or discrete-target assumption is needed.

headlines.title: Characters of binary products
headlines.text:
Restriction gives
`PontryaginDual.prodEquiv A B : PontryaginDual (A × B) ≃ₜ*
(PontryaginDual A × PontryaginDual B)`; the inverse sends `(χ, ψ)` to
`(a, b) ↦ χ a * ψ b`. The source monoids have their original, arbitrary
topologies, with no operation-continuity, local-compactness or separation
assumption. The equivalence uses the entire compact-open character spaces
and is natural under products of continuous monoid homomorphisms. More
generally, the compact-open coproduct equivalence for continuous
homomorphisms has a commutative topological-group target; its algebraic
restriction universal property needs only a commutative-monoid target with
continuous multiplication. See
[`ContinuousMonoidHom`](https://github.com/FormalFrontier/group-theory/blob/cad97f1a1920e3c68d41ec2d689cde51231b5a31/GroupTheory/Topology/Algebra/ContinuousMonoidHom.lean)
and [`PontryaginDual.Prod`](https://github.com/FormalFrontier/group-theory/blob/cad97f1a1920e3c68d41ec2d689cde51231b5a31/GroupTheory/Topology/PontryaginDual/Prod.lean).
This binary result asserts neither infinite-product duality nor bidual reflexivity.

headlines.title: Canonical biduality of binary products and the real plane
headlines.text:
`PontryaginDual.evalHom A : A →* PontryaginDual (PontryaginDual A)` bundles
fixed evaluation for any monoid with a topology. Given factor equivalences
`eA : A ≃ₜ* PontryaginDual (PontryaginDual A)` and `eB` with the pointwise
laws `eA a χ = χ a` and `eB b ψ = ψ b`, `PontryaginDual.prodEvalEquiv`
has evaluation as its forward map and an explicit inverse using the two
supplied inverses and the product-dual comparison. No additional local
compactness, group, separation or operation-continuity hypotheses are needed.
`ContinuousMulEquiv.prodMultiplicative` lifts Mathlib's algebraic
tag-of-product equivalence under addition and topologies alone.
`PontryaginDual.realPlaneEvalEquiv` applies the product construction to the
two real factors and this tag equivalence, on `Multiplicative (ℝ × ℝ)` with
its original topology. The binary construction allows one-point factors;
no positive-dimension or nontriviality assumption is imposed.
See [`PontryaginDual.Prod`](https://github.com/FormalFrontier/group-theory/blob/cad97f1a1920e3c68d41ec2d689cde51231b5a31/GroupTheory/Topology/PontryaginDual/Prod.lean),
[`TypeTags`](https://github.com/FormalFrontier/group-theory/blob/cad97f1a1920e3c68d41ec2d689cde51231b5a31/GroupTheory/Topology/TypeTags.lean) and
[`PontryaginDual.Real`](https://github.com/FormalFrontier/group-theory/blob/cad97f1a1920e3c68d41ec2d689cde51231b5a31/GroupTheory/Topology/PontryaginDual/Real.lean).
This is not an assertion of infinite-product or
general locally compact abelian biduality.

headlines.title: Finite dependent products and finite real function spaces
headlines.text:
For a finite index
`I` and monoids `A i` with topologies, `PontryaginDual.piEquiv A` identifies
`PontryaginDual (∀ i, A i)` with `∀ i, PontryaginDual (A i)`, using their entire
compact-open duals. Restriction uses the identity-supported coordinate
inclusions; the inverse has value `∏ i, χ i (a i)`. The more general
`ContinuousMonoidHom.piEquiv A E` has a commutative topological group target
`E`; the source factors need no continuous operations, commutativity, local
compactness or separation. Supplied canonical factor bidual equivalences and
their evaluation laws give `PontryaginDual.piEvalEquiv A e h`, with forward
map exactly evaluation and inverse given by the supplied coordinate inverses.
`ContinuousMulEquiv.piMultiplicative A` lifts Mathlib's algebraic tag
equivalence for any index under addition and topologies alone.
`PontryaginDual.realPiEvalEquiv I` then gives canonical biduality on the original
`Multiplicative (I → ℝ)` for every finite `I`, including the empty index and
hence dimension zero. This real-case consequence is auxiliary to the duality
setting of Neukirch–Schmidt–Wingberg. No infinite-product or general locally
compact abelian duality theorem is asserted. See
[`ContinuousMonoidHom.Pi`](https://github.com/FormalFrontier/group-theory/blob/cad97f1a1920e3c68d41ec2d689cde51231b5a31/GroupTheory/Topology/Algebra/ContinuousMonoidHom/Pi.lean),
[`PontryaginDual.Pi`](https://github.com/FormalFrontier/group-theory/blob/cad97f1a1920e3c68d41ec2d689cde51231b5a31/GroupTheory/Topology/PontryaginDual/Pi.lean) and
[`PontryaginDual.Real`](https://github.com/FormalFrontier/group-theory/blob/cad97f1a1920e3c68d41ec2d689cde51231b5a31/GroupTheory/Topology/PontryaginDual/Real.lean).
The finite algebraic universal property reuses Mathlib's work of Joachim
Breitner and Yakov Pechersky; the coordinate and tag equivalences reuse the
Mathlib formalizations credited in those modules.

headlines.title: Integer characters by generator evaluation
headlines.text:
For any topological group
`E`, `ContinuousMonoidHom.intEvalHomeomorph E` identifies the compact-open
space `Multiplicative ℤ →ₜ* E` with `E`, by evaluation at
`Multiplicative.ofAdd (1 : ℤ)`. The inverse sends `e` to the continuous
homomorphism with underlying map `zpowersHom E e`, taking `n` to
`e ^ n.toAdd`. For commutative `E`, `ContinuousMonoidHom.intEvalEquiv E`
is a continuous multiplicative equivalence with the same homeomorphism.
No local compactness or Hausdorff hypothesis is needed. Specializing to
`Circle` identifies the whole `PontryaginDual (Multiplicative ℤ)` with
`Circle`. The characteristic laws and target naturality are in
[`ContinuousMonoidHom.Int`](https://github.com/FormalFrontier/group-theory/blob/cad97f1a1920e3c68d41ec2d689cde51231b5a31/GroupTheory/Topology/Algebra/ContinuousMonoidHom/Int.lean),
which reuses Mathlib's integer universal property and compact-open continuity
results, with the formalization credits listed in its references.

**[Complete headline catalogue: statements, hypotheses and module links](https://github.com/FormalFrontier/group-theory/blob/cad97f1a1920e3c68d41ec2d689cde51231b5a31/docs/HeadlineResults.md).**
The families below give an overview; the catalogue retains the full statements
and qualifications. For API details and examples, see the
[result guide](https://github.com/FormalFrontier/group-theory/blob/cad97f1a1920e3c68d41ec2d689cde51231b5a31/docs/Results.md); for imports and applications, see the
[usage guide](https://github.com/FormalFrontier/group-theory/blob/cad97f1a1920e3c68d41ec2d689cde51231b5a31/docs/Usage.md).

headlines.title: Zero-sum pairs and multiplicative images
headlines.text:
In a nonunital, nonassociative semiring, `a + b = 0` implies `a * a = b * b`.
A multiplication-preserving function into any monoid sends `a` and `b` to
units simultaneously, without preserving addition, zero or one or requiring
commutativity of the target. See the
[zero-sum API](https://github.com/FormalFrontier/group-theory/blob/cad97f1a1920e3c68d41ec2d689cde51231b5a31/GroupTheory/Algebra/IsAddUnit.lean).

headlines.title: Cyclic products in a monoid with zero satisfy `nilpotencyClass (a * b) ≤ nilpotencyClass (b * a) + 1`, and symmetrically
headlines.text:
Cyclic products in a monoid with zero satisfy
`nilpotencyClass (a * b) ≤ nilpotencyClass (b * a) + 1`, and symmetrically; see
[nilpotency classes](https://github.com/FormalFrontier/group-theory/blob/cad97f1a1920e3c68d41ec2d689cde51231b5a31/GroupTheory/Algebra/GroupWithZero/Nilpotent.lean).

In a reduced ring, not necessarily commutative, equality at two coprime natural
powers determines an element; equality at two exponents is equivalent to equality
at their gcd. In a reduced monoid with zero, positive powers preserve left and
right annihilators. Aligned lists of positive powers preserve product-zero, not
product values. See the [complete statements](https://github.com/FormalFrontier/group-theory/blob/cad97f1a1920e3c68d41ec2d689cde51231b5a31/docs/HeadlineResults.md#further-algebraic-and-character-results)
and the [reduced-ring power API](https://github.com/FormalFrontier/group-theory/blob/cad97f1a1920e3c68d41ec2d689cde51231b5a31/GroupTheory/Ring/Power.lean).
Over a commutative ring, equality of two powers modulo a radical ideal is
equivalent to equality at their gcd, including zero exponents; see the
[radical-ideal API](https://github.com/FormalFrontier/group-theory/blob/cad97f1a1920e3c68d41ec2d689cde51231b5a31/GroupTheory/Ring/Ideal/Power.lean).

In any monoid with zero, `nilpotencyClass_pow` gives
`nilpotencyClass (a ^ n) = (nilpotencyClass a + n - 1) / n` for every natural
exponent, using total natural-number division at zero. Unital monoid maps preserving and
reflecting zero preserve the class; injectivity is not required. See
[`Algebra.GroupWithZero.Nilpotent`](https://github.com/FormalFrontier/group-theory/blob/cad97f1a1920e3c68d41ec2d689cde51231b5a31/GroupTheory/Algebra/GroupWithZero/Nilpotent.lean).
Separately, `SemiconjBy a x a` and nilpotence of `x` bound the
nilpotency class of `a` by that of `x` plus one. Finite pairwise orthogonal sums
over any semiring are nilpotent exactly when every supported summand is nilpotent,
with an explicit class bound. For finite pairwise commuting families with
`f i ^ n i = 0`, the sum vanishes to the power `1 + ∑ i ∈ s, (n i - 1)`.
No commutativity or nontriviality of the semiring, positivity of the individual
exponents, or finite index type is assumed. The
[catalogue](https://github.com/FormalFrontier/group-theory/blob/cad97f1a1920e3c68d41ec2d689cde51231b5a31/docs/HeadlineResults.md#further-algebraic-and-character-results) records
empty-support cases and the class-zero convention for nonnilpotent elements;
these results use [`Ring.Nilpotent.Finset`](https://github.com/FormalFrontier/group-theory/blob/cad97f1a1920e3c68d41ec2d689cde51231b5a31/GroupTheory/Ring/Nilpotent/Finset.lean).

For a semiring algebra over a commutative semiring, a finite sum of pairwise
commuting submodules has total nilpotency class at most one plus the sum of the
predecessors of the summands' total classes. A finite span satisfies the corresponding
generator-class bound when the generators' principal submodules pairwise commute;
the generators themselves need not commute. Neither bound assumes summand or
generator nilpotence, and both include empty support and trivial carriers. See the
[finite-submodule bounds](https://github.com/FormalFrontier/group-theory/blob/cad97f1a1920e3c68d41ec2d689cde51231b5a31/GroupTheory/Ring/Nilpotent/Submodule.lean).

Over a commutative semiring `R`, the finitely generated ideal criterion
`Ideal.FG.isNilpotent_iff_le_nilradical` characterizes nilpotence by containment
in the nilradical. The finite-span bound specializes to
`nilpotencyClass (Ideal.span (↑s : Set R)) ≤ 1 + ∑ x ∈ s, (nilpotencyClass x - 1)`.
Nonnilpotent ideals have total class zero, so this upper bound alone is not a
nilpotence criterion. See the [finite-ideal API](https://github.com/FormalFrontier/group-theory/blob/cad97f1a1920e3c68d41ec2d689cde51231b5a31/GroupTheory/Ring/Nilpotent/Ideal.lean).

For commuting elements `a, c` in any monoid, `a ∣ c` implies
`a ^ n ∣ c ^ n` for every natural `n`, including zero. In a monoid with zero,
if `a` is nilpotent, the commuting multiple has nilpotency class at most that of
`a`. In particular this bounds a product `a * b` when `a` commutes with `b`,
and a list product when the nilpotent `a` occurs in the list and commutes with
every entry. Other entries need not be nilpotent or commute with one another.
These bounds retain the nilpotence premise: the total class is zero for
nonnilpotent elements, so a class inequality alone is not a nilpotence criterion.
See the [commuting-divisor API](https://github.com/FormalFrontier/group-theory/blob/cad97f1a1920e3c68d41ec2d689cde51231b5a31/GroupTheory/Algebra/Divisibility/Basic.lean),
[list-product API](https://github.com/FormalFrontier/group-theory/blob/cad97f1a1920e3c68d41ec2d689cde51231b5a31/GroupTheory/Algebra/BigOperators/GroupWithZero/List.lean) and
[full statements](https://github.com/FormalFrontier/group-theory/blob/cad97f1a1920e3c68d41ec2d689cde51231b5a31/docs/HeadlineResults.md#further-algebraic-and-character-results).

headlines.title: Finite sums and product homomorphisms
headlines.text:
For submodules of a semiring equipped with a module structure over another
semiring, `Submodule.sum_eq_sup` identifies finite sums with finite suprema,
complementing the zero/bottom and addition/supremum identities.
No scalar-tower, commutativity, or algebra hypothesis is required. See
[`Algebra.Algebra.Operations`](https://github.com/FormalFrontier/group-theory/blob/cad97f1a1920e3c68d41ec2d689cde51231b5a31/GroupTheory/Algebra/Algebra/Operations.lean).

Finite families of nonunital ring homomorphisms whose distinct images annihilate
each other in both orders have a sum homomorphism, even for nonunital,
nonassociative source and target semirings. For a finite dependent product of
unital nonassociative semirings, `Pi.liftRingHom` instead builds a **unital**
homomorphism into an associative semiring from nonunital component maps: their
unit images must be pairwise orthogonal and sum to one. No commutativity, global
centrality or nontriviality is assumed. The empty-index case is included; its
cover-one premise forces the target to satisfy `0 = 1`. See
[`Ring.Hom.FiniteSum`](https://github.com/FormalFrontier/group-theory/blob/cad97f1a1920e3c68d41ec2d689cde51231b5a31/GroupTheory/Ring/Hom/FiniteSum.lean) and the
[catalogue](https://github.com/FormalFrontier/group-theory/blob/cad97f1a1920e3c68d41ec2d689cde51231b5a31/docs/HeadlineResults.md#further-algebraic-and-character-results) for
application, zero-off extension and uniqueness laws, with their hypotheses.

headlines.title: Power restrictions and order
headlines.text:
In any group, membership of every power in a finite family in a subgroup-like
object is equivalent to membership of the gcd power; gcd one detects the element.
The subgroup generated by the selected powers is the cyclic subgroup generated
by that gcd power. Additive groups have the corresponding natural-multiple
formulas. No commutativity or normality is needed; empty and all-zero families
generate the trivial subgroup. See the
[subgroup-power API](https://github.com/FormalFrontier/group-theory/blob/cad97f1a1920e3c68d41ec2d689cde51231b5a31/GroupTheory/Algebra/Group/Subgroup/Power.lean).

For any group element `a` and natural exponents `m n`, the intersection of
`Subgroup.zpowers (a ^ m)` and `Subgroup.zpowers (a ^ n)` is
`Subgroup.zpowers (a ^ (Nat.lcm m n))`. The additive version uses the
integer-multiple subgroups of `m • a` and `n • a`. Zero exponents are included;
no commutativity or order assumption is needed. See the same
[subgroup-power API](https://github.com/FormalFrontier/group-theory/blob/cad97f1a1920e3c68d41ec2d689cde51231b5a31/GroupTheory/Algebra/Group/Subgroup/Power.lean).

For a finite family of natural exponents, intersecting the cyclic power subgroups
with `Subgroup.zpowers a` gives the subgroup generated by the lcm power.
Nonempty families need no initial cyclic factor; for an empty family the plain
intersection is top. Additive groups have the corresponding natural-multiple
formula. See the [catalogue](https://github.com/FormalFrontier/group-theory/blob/cad97f1a1920e3c68d41ec2d689cde51231b5a31/docs/HeadlineResults.md#power-restrictions-and-order).

In a monoid, let `a` have injective left multiplication (left regularity).
Equality of its powers and those of arbitrary `b` at a finite family of natural
exponents is equivalent to equality at their gcd;
a family with gcd one determines `a = b`. The same finite-family criterion
holds separately when `a` has injective right multiplication (right regularity).
No regularity of `b` or global cancellation is needed; additive versions hold in
additive monoids. Empty families and zero exponents are included. See the
[power-kernel API](https://github.com/FormalFrontier/group-theory/blob/cad97f1a1920e3c68d41ec2d689cde51231b5a31/GroupTheory/MonoidHom/PositivePower.lean).

Let `f : M →* N`, where `N` is a monoid and `M` has only multiplication and a
chosen one (`MulOne`). If the range of `f` contains a positive power of every
element of `N`, it detects equality of homomorphisms from `N` into any monoid
with unique positive roots.

For finite image detection, let `f : A →* M`, with only `MulOne A` and monoids
`M, N`. Suppose each `x : M` admits `s : Finset ι` and `e : ι → ℕ` with
`s.gcd e = 1` and `x ^ (e i) ∈ Set.range f` for every `i ∈ s`. For fixed
`g h : M →* N`, left-regularity of every `g x` gives
`g.comp f = h.comp f ↔ g = h`; a separate criterion uses right-regularity
instead. In both, `h` is arbitrary, the four universes are independent, and
`s, e` may depend on `x`. Additive peers use `AddZero A`, additive monoids
and natural multiples.
No global cancellation, commutativity, group structure, surjectivity, positivity,
finite or nonempty index type, or decidable equality is assumed. Zero and
repeated exponents are allowed; empty or all-zero families cannot have gcd one.
The natural-set left interface is the `ι = ℕ`, `e = id` specialization;
coprime and consecutive-power adapters remain available. Consecutive-power
images give precomposition injectivity into left-cancellative targets.
The [catalogue](https://github.com/FormalFrontier/group-theory/blob/cad97f1a1920e3c68d41ec2d689cde51231b5a31/docs/HeadlineResults.md#power-restrictions-and-order) distinguishes
these fixed-pair image criteria from elementwise power kernels and injectivity
on all homomorphisms into an arbitrary monoid.

More generally, a set of a monoid that contains, for each element, a finite
family of its powers with gcd-one exponents detects equality of fixed
multiplication-preserving maps into a monoid whenever the first map has
left-regular values. Unit preservation and regularity of the second map are not
required. The [set criterion and additive form](https://github.com/FormalFrontier/group-theory/blob/cad97f1a1920e3c68d41ec2d689cde51231b5a31/docs/HeadlineResults.md#further-algebraic-and-character-results)
allow independent universes, element-dependent families and zero or repeated exponents.

For a multiplicatively Archimedean commutative monoid with a linear order,
chosen `0`, `0 ≤ 1` and strictly monotone multiplication by positive elements,
a multiplication-closed set is bounded above exactly when all its members are
at most `1`, even for empty sets. See the
[power and order catalogue](https://github.com/FormalFrontier/group-theory/blob/cad97f1a1920e3c68d41ec2d689cde51231b5a31/docs/HeadlineResults.md#power-restrictions-and-order)
for additive restriction, pointwise comparison and multiplicative-map versions.

headlines.title: Group actions and presentations
headlines.text:
For a commutative ring `R`, a commutative domain `A` with an `R`-algebra
structure, and a monoid `M` acting on `A` by semiring endomorphisms,
`IsIntegral.finite_orbit` proves that every element integral over `R` has
finite orbit, provided `[SMulCommClass M R A]`. The three types may lie in
independent universes. Scalar commutation fixes the image of `R`; no action
on `R`, injective scalar map, faithful action, integrality of all of `A`,
or group or finiteness assumption on `M` is required. See
[`GroupAction.Integral`](https://github.com/FormalFrontier/group-theory/blob/cad97f1a1920e3c68d41ec2d689cde51231b5a31/GroupTheory/GroupAction/Integral.lean) and the
[finite-orbit API](https://github.com/FormalFrontier/group-theory/blob/cad97f1a1920e3c68d41ec2d689cde51231b5a31/docs/Results.md#finite-orbits-of-integral-elements).

For arbitrary subgroups `H, K` of a group `G`, equivariant maps `G/H → G/K`
exist exactly when `H ≤ gKg⁻¹` for some `g`; the coset actions are isomorphic
exactly when the subgroups are conjugate, not merely when maps exist both ways.
Group-valued diagrams have presentations by free products modulo the normal
closure of arrow relations. For a group homomorphism `f : A →* B`, a pushout
along `A → T` with `T` trivial is `B / normalClosure (range f)`.
Objectwise-surjective compatible homomorphisms between two diagrams over the same
arbitrary indexing category induce a surjection of colimits; its kernel is the
normal closure of the component kernels' images. The object groups may have
independent universes.
The [actions and presentations catalogue](https://github.com/FormalFrontier/group-theory/blob/cad97f1a1920e3c68d41ec2d689cde51231b5a31/docs/HeadlineResults.md#group-actions-and-presentations)
also gives coefficient-sum relations over semirings and the precise universal
properties, including their universe qualifications.

headlines.title: Fixed vectors and averaging
headlines.text:
For monoid representations on additive commutative monoid modules over a
semiring, intertwiners `f, g` with injective `f` and `Function.Exact f g` remain
exact on fixed submodules. Fixed vectors commute with arbitrary products and
algebraic direct sums, but do not in general preserve surjectivity.

**[Noetherian monoid cohomology](https://github.com/FormalFrontier/group-theory/blob/cad97f1a1920e3c68d41ec2d689cde51231b5a31/GroupTheory/Cohomology/Noetherian.lean).**
For `A : Rep R G` over any ring `R` and monoid `G`,
[inhomogeneous cochains](https://github.com/FormalFrontier/group-theory/blob/cad97f1a1920e3c68d41ec2d689cde51231b5a31/GroupTheory/Cohomology/Basic.lean) have degree `n`
term `(Fin n → G) → A` and differential using the given linear action.
Degree zero is canonically `R`-linearly equivalent to `A.ρ.fixedSubmodule`.
If `IsNoetherian R A`, degree-zero cohomology is Noetherian for arbitrary `G`;
if also `Finite G`, cohomology is Noetherian in every natural degree.
Neither commutativity nor Noetherianity of `R`, finiteness of the underlying
`A`, nor a trivial action is required. The [catalogue](https://github.com/FormalFrontier/group-theory/blob/cad97f1a1920e3c68d41ec2d689cde51231b5a31/docs/HeadlineResults.md#fixed-vectors-and-averaging)
gives the independent universes and the narrower Mathlib group-cohomology comparison.

For a finite group whose order is a unit in a possibly noncommutative semiring,
a given linear lift between intertwining maps can be replaced by an
intertwining lift; no surjectivity of the map lifted through is required.
Separately, for a finite group acting by additive automorphisms on an additive
commutative group, bijective multiplication by the group order makes every
crossed map principal. The [fixed-vector and averaging catalogue](https://github.com/FormalFrontier/group-theory/blob/cad97f1a1920e3c68d41ec2d689cde51231b5a31/docs/HeadlineResults.md#fixed-vectors-and-averaging)
keeps the representation and additive-action hypotheses distinct and gives the
explicit averaging formula and its naturality.

A pretransitive group action on a finite nonempty set has permutation-fixed
submodule linearly equivalent to the coefficient semiring; the acting group need
not be finite and no invertible order is needed. A nonzero fixed vector forces
the acted-on carrier to be finite; on an infinite pretransitive carrier the fixed
submodule is bottom, still over any coefficient semiring. Separately, for a finite group
whose order is a unit in a possibly noncommutative semiring, the normalized norm
is a natural idempotent self-intertwiner with range the fixed submodule, on
additive commutative monoid modules. Its narrower commutative-ring comparison
with Mathlib's `averageMap` is in the
[catalogue](https://github.com/FormalFrontier/group-theory/blob/cad97f1a1920e3c68d41ec2d689cde51231b5a31/docs/HeadlineResults.md#further-algebraic-and-character-results).

headlines.title: Free groups, arithmetic and Grothendieck completions
headlines.text:
For any generator relabeling `σ : I → J`, the kernel of `FreeGroup.map σ` is
the **normal closure** of all `of i * (of k)⁻¹` with `σ i = σ k`. The label
types may be empty and lie in independent universes; no injectivity, surjectivity
or finiteness is needed. The induced homomorphism is injective or surjective
exactly when `σ` is. See the [free-group map API](https://github.com/FormalFrontier/group-theory/blob/cad97f1a1920e3c68d41ec2d689cde51231b5a31/GroupTheory/FreeGroup/Map.lean).

For a finite-index subgroup `H` of a finitely generated free group `G`,
`rank H + [G:H] = rank G * [G:H] + 1`, including ambient rank zero.
Mathlib supplies subgroup freeness and finite generation. Biadditive maps from
two additive commutative monoids to an additive commutative group extend uniquely
to both Grothendieck completions; a semiring's additive completion has a canonical
ring structure and universal ring lifts, without cancellation.

For a finitely generated additive commutative group `M`, a subgroup has finite
index exactly when its canonical integer-module finrank equals `Module.finrank ℤ M`.
The [finite-index criterion](https://github.com/FormalFrontier/group-theory/blob/cad97f1a1920e3c68d41ec2d689cde51231b5a31/GroupTheory/FiniteIndex.lean) requires
`[Module.Finite ℤ M]`, not freeness or torsion-freeness, and includes rank zero.
The span of a linearly independent family of `Module.finrank ℤ M` elements has
finite quotient and positive subgroup index.

For an additive commutative group `V`, subgroup `L` and natural `n`, bijective
multiplication by `n` on `V` gives `(V/L)[n] ≃+ L/nL`. If `L` is finitely generated,
this torsion subgroup is finite of cardinality `n ^ Module.finrank ℤ L`, without
freeness of `L` or ambient finite generation. The
[free-group, arithmetic and completion catalogue](https://github.com/FormalFrontier/group-theory/blob/cad97f1a1920e3c68d41ec2d689cde51231b5a31/docs/HeadlineResults.md#free-groups-arithmetic-and-grothendieck-completions)
also links the explicit index-two generators and nilpotence reflection on additive units.

headlines.title: Topology and abstract homomorphisms
headlines.text:
**Continuous endomorphisms of additive circles.** For every nonzero real `T`,
`AddCircle.continuousAddMonoidHomEquivInt` is an additive equivalence from
continuous additive endomorphisms of `AddCircle T`, with pointwise addition,
to `ℤ`. Its inverse sends `n` to `n • id`, pointwise `x ↦ n • x`;
equivalently, every such `F` satisfies `F x = n • x` for all `x`, for a
unique integer `n`. See the
[endomorphism module](https://github.com/FormalFrontier/group-theory/blob/cad97f1a1920e3c68d41ec2d689cde51231b5a31/GroupTheory/Topology/AddCircle/Endomorphisms.lean).

**Compact subsemigroups and submonoids.** In a group with a given topology
and continuous fixed left translations, a closed compact subsemigroup `S`
satisfies `x ∈ S → x⁻¹ ∈ S`. Every element of a closed compact submonoid is
a unit in that submonoid. In particular, a compact submonoid of a Hausdorff
topological group has the same carrier as a subgroup, since compact subsets
are closed. The closed compact results require neither continuous right
translations nor continuous inversion. The versions for closed subsemigroups
and submonoids with Noetherian induced topology follow from compactness. See
the [subsemigroup module](https://github.com/FormalFrontier/group-theory/blob/cad97f1a1920e3c68d41ec2d689cde51231b5a31/GroupTheory/Topology/Algebra/Group/Subsemigroup.lean).

For a subsemigroup `S` of a group with continuous fixed left translations,
its topological closure is stable under inverses if that closure's induced
topology is Noetherian and each right translation by a member of `S` is
continuous on the closure. No ambient Noetherianity or continuous inversion is
assumed. See
[`Subsemigroup.inv_mem_closure_of_noetherianSpace`](https://github.com/FormalFrontier/group-theory/blob/cad97f1a1920e3c68d41ec2d689cde51231b5a31/GroupTheory/Topology/Algebra/Group/Subsemigroup/Closure.lean)
and the [precise inputs](https://github.com/FormalFrontier/group-theory/blob/cad97f1a1920e3c68d41ec2d689cde51231b5a31/docs/Usage.md#inverses-in-a-subsemigroups-closure).
Alternatively, with the same local right continuity, inverse stability follows
if `S` is preirreducible and strict inclusion of nonempty irreducible closed
subsets of the ambient group is well-founded (`WellFoundedLT`). This applies to
every element of the closure, not just members of `S`.

More generally, a closed self-embedding of any topological space is surjective
if the space has finitely many irreducible components and well-founded strict
inclusion of nonempty irreducible closed subsets. No Noetherianity or separation is assumed;
see the [closed-embedding theorem](https://github.com/FormalFrontier/group-theory/blob/cad97f1a1920e3c68d41ec2d689cde51231b5a31/GroupTheory/Topology/ClosedEmbedding.lean).

In a compact Hausdorff commutative topological group with a dense algebraically
finitely generated subgroup, every abstract finite-index subgroup is open.
Every abstract homomorphism from such a source to a compact nonarchimedean group
is continuous, even with an infinite image; this does not assert local constancy.
The [topology catalogue](https://github.com/FormalFrontier/group-theory/blob/cad97f1a1920e3c68d41ec2d689cde51231b5a31/docs/HeadlineResults.md#topology-and-abstract-homomorphisms)
also covers ultrafilter-limit counterexamples to continuity, cofinite groups and
actions, locally constructible subgroups, identity components, compact open
subgroups and finite-coordinate factorizations.

Two continuity interfaces are separate: a pretransitive group action by continuous
fixed-element maps on a finite T0 space makes its given topology discrete, with
no topology or finiteness needed on the group. By contrast, for topological spaces
`M, X` where every point of `X` has a finite neighborhood, a primitive scalar
operation `M × X → X` is jointly continuous if **both** fixed-scalar maps and orbit
maps are continuous; no action laws or separation are required.
The catalogue includes the local finite-neighborhood criterion for arbitrary maps.

headlines.title: Saturation of uniformly spanning character sets
headlines.text:
Let `K` be a compact
monoid with measurable opens and measurable fixed translations, and let `μ`
be a finite nonzero left-invariant measure. If the complex span of the scalar
characters from a set `S` is uniformly dense in `C(K, ℂ)`, then `S` is the
entire Pontryagin dual. In particular, every point-separating subgroup of
characters is the whole dual. The measure need not be a probability measure;
no group, Hausdorffness or countability assumption on `K` is required. See
[`PontryaginDual.Saturation`](https://github.com/FormalFrontier/group-theory/blob/cad97f1a1920e3c68d41ec2d689cde51231b5a31/GroupTheory/Topology/PontryaginDual/Saturation.lean).

headlines.title: Uniform density of scalar characters
headlines.text:
Let `K` be a compact monoid with a
topology, and let `S` be a subgroup of its continuous `Circle`-valued
characters that separates points of `K`. The complex linear span of
`x ↦ (χ x : ℂ)`, for `χ ∈ S`, is dense in `C(K, ℂ)` for the uniform topology.
No measure, continuity of the monoid operations, or separation or countability
typeclass on `K` is required. This uses Mathlib's scalar Stone–Weierstrass theorem;
see [`GroupTheory.Topology.PontryaginDual.StoneWeierstrass`](https://github.com/FormalFrontier/group-theory/blob/cad97f1a1920e3c68d41ec2d689cde51231b5a31/GroupTheory/Topology/PontryaginDual/StoneWeierstrass.lean).

headlines.title: Real characters and canonical biduality
headlines.text:
Every continuous circle-valued
character of the additive real line has a unique period-one Fourier frequency.
`PontryaginDual.realEquiv` identifies the original real topology with the
compact-open topology on the entire real character space. The forward map of
`PontryaginDual.realEvalEquiv` is canonical bidual evaluation, not a separately
chosen algebraic identification. See
[`PontryaginDual.Real`](https://github.com/FormalFrontier/group-theory/blob/cad97f1a1920e3c68d41ec2d689cde51231b5a31/GroupTheory/Topology/PontryaginDual/Real.lean).

headlines.title: Transport of the whole Pontryagin dual
headlines.text:
A continuous multiplicative
equivalence `A ≃ₜ* B` induces `PontryaginDual B ≃ₜ* PontryaginDual A` by
precomposition, with the original compact-open topologies. Only monoids with
topologies are needed: no local compactness, Hausdorffness or continuity of
their operations is assumed. See `PontryaginDual.mapEquiv` in
[`PontryaginDual`](https://github.com/FormalFrontier/group-theory/blob/cad97f1a1920e3c68d41ec2d689cde51231b5a31/GroupTheory/Topology/PontryaginDual.lean).

headlines.title: Canonical Pontryagin bidual evaluation
headlines.text:
For a monoid `A` equipped with a
topology and `[LocallyCompactPair A Circle]`, `PontryaginDual.eval A` is the
continuous homomorphism `a ↦ (χ ↦ χ a)` into the existing compact-open bidual.
It is natural under arbitrary continuous monoid homomorphisms. If the dual
also forms a locally compact pair with `Circle`, evaluation on the dual is
a section of the dual of evaluation. No group, commutativity, continuity of
the monoid operations or Hausdorff hypothesis on `A` is required. These
general monoid results alone do not assert injectivity, surjectivity or full Pontryagin reflexivity
of the original evaluation. See
[`GroupTheory.Topology.PontryaginDual`](https://github.com/FormalFrontier/group-theory/blob/cad97f1a1920e3c68d41ec2d689cde51231b5a31/GroupTheory/Topology/PontryaginDual.lean).

headlines.title: Bidual evaluation separates discrete abelian groups
headlines.text:
For a commutative
group with its discrete topology, `PontryaginDual.eval_injective_of_discrete`
proves that the canonical continuous bidual evaluation is injective. No
finiteness, finite generation or countability is required. The injectivity
theorem is available in
[`PontryaginDual.Discrete`](https://github.com/FormalFrontier/group-theory/blob/cad97f1a1920e3c68d41ec2d689cde51231b5a31/GroupTheory/Topology/PontryaginDual/Discrete.lean).
For full canonical continuous reflexivity, including the inverse, use
`PontryaginDual.evalEquivOfDiscrete` in
[`PontryaginDual.Discrete.Equivalence`](https://github.com/FormalFrontier/group-theory/blob/cad97f1a1920e3c68d41ec2d689cde51231b5a31/GroupTheory/Topology/PontryaginDual/Discrete/Equivalence.lean).

headlines.title: Integrals and orthogonality of characters
headlines.text:
For a monoid `K` with its original
topology and measurable space, measurable opens and `[MeasurableMul K]`,
a nontrivial continuous circle-valued character has complex Bochner integral zero
against any left-invariant measure. Distinct characters have zero off-diagonal
integral `∫ x, χ x * conj (ψ x) ∂μ`.
No group, compactness, finiteness or normalization of the measure is assumed;
for a nonintegrable function the Bochner integral is zero by definition.
See `PontryaginDual.integral_eq_zero_of_ne_one` and `integral_mul_conj_eq_zero`
in [`PontryaginDual.Integral`](https://github.com/FormalFrontier/group-theory/blob/cad97f1a1920e3c68d41ec2d689cde51231b5a31/GroupTheory/Topology/PontryaginDual/Integral.lean).
